reason: No official French source publishes a take-home (net a payer) or median net monthly wage statistic for graduates, or for employees at all. Established positively, not by failure to find a page: the official French data portal INSEE publishes gross wage distributions and, for its wage statistics, publishes DECILES rather than take-home, because its wage data are collected as gross; the official income-tax authority impots.gouv.fr publishes the withholding rate grids (archived in FR/021_net_monthly_income_pas_grille_officielle.json) and a net imposable calculator, but no net a payer table; the official social security portal service-public.fr publishes employee contribution rates and bases (archived in FR/020_net_monthly_income.json) but no net a payer table. No French authority publishes a gross-to-net conversion table, so the figure the corpus holds has to be DERIVED from those two official component sets rather than quoted as a published net. The derivation is recorded in FR/020_net_monthly_income.json (net a payer EUR 2,205.69 per month from EUR 2,800.53 gross) and is usable. What does not exist is the thing this file would otherwise have supplied: an official published median take-home figure.
what_blocked_it: The components are all published; the composite is not. France's payroll disclosure rules require the payslip to DISCLOSE the net (montant net a payer) rather than require any authority to PUBLISH it, so the authoritative net figure exists only per payslip and is never aggregated by an official body. The Ministry of Solidarity does publish a national 'montant net social' measure, but that is deliberately defined as gross minus only the statutory compulsory employee contributions, i.e. it excludes income tax and is therefore NOT take-home. Using it as a net monthly income figure would have been exactly the gross-as-net substitution this corpus forbids. Separately, INSEE's gross wage statistics cannot be converted to net without the withheld amounts, which are not published, and even if they were, the net depends on household composition through the quotient familial, so there is no single national net figure even in principle without further assumptions.
recommended_handling: Use the derived figure in FR/020_net_monthly_income.json and label it DERIVED, not official-published. State the gross input alongside it in every place it appears. Do not substitute the 'montant net social' measure for take-home. Do not average the metropolitan and overseas PAS grids, and state clearly that the figure covers metropolitan France.
raw_extract: From the Ministry of Solidarity payslip guidance, defining the measures so this negative result can be checked: 'le "net a payer", qui figure le plus souvent en bas du bulletin de paie, correspond au montant effectivement verse au salarie par l'employeur et doit permettre au salarie de verifier que l'ensemble des calculs sont exacts. Ce montant tient compte de toutes les deductions, notamment de l'ensemble des cotisations sociales et du prelevement a la source, mais prend egalement en compte certains elements annexes (ex : saisies sur salaires, remboursement de frais professionnels, participation du salarie aux titres restaurants, retenue pour la cantine, etc.) qui ne correspondent pas a des revenus ou a des charges deductibles. Figure egalement sur le bulletin de paye, pour rappel, le "net a payer avant impot", qui correspond a la somme nette a payer qu'aurait percue le salarie si le prelevement a la source de l'impot sur le revenu n'avait pas ete mis en place depuis 2019. Cette deuxieme information est donc donnee pour simple information ;' and 'le revenu "net fiscal" (ou "net imposable") correspond aux sommes soumises au prelevement a la source de l'impot sur le revenu.'

field_mapping.net_monthly_income: fr.career.net_monthly_income - no published official value; see FR/020_net_monthly_income.json for the derived value

notes: This file records an absence of evidence, which is itself evidence worth archiving: the corpus must not silently upgrade a derived French figure to an official one, and must not adopt the 'montant net social' as a take-home proxy. The raw_extract is included so that a future researcher can confirm from an official source that 'net a payer', 'net a payer avant impot' and 'net imposable' are three different quantities, and therefore that any single French 'net salary' figure is ambiguous until one of the three is named.
evidence_limitations: A negative finding. It records that no official published take-home statistic was found for France as of 2026-10-05; it does not assert that no such figure has ever existed or that none could be produced later. The list of attempted sources is what I personally fetched or read; other official routes, such as a data request to INSEE or a bespoke CASSE-order extract from URSSAF, were not pursued and could in principle yield aggregated figures.
